stories.headline: Ohio votes put three Amazon data-centre plans at risk
stories.confirmed_fact: Ohio voters backed 21 local measures restricting or scrutinising data-centre developments in the 3 November election. Financial Times research identifies three affected Amazon projects, representing more than $17 billion in planned spending and roughly 1.8 gigawatts of proposed power demand. The projects face potential delay or cancellation; they have not all been definitively stopped.
stories.why_it_matters: Planning consent, electricity demand and local trust can disrupt infrastructure investment even when the financing is available. Residents have raised concerns about noise, pollution, energy costs and how projects are negotiated.
stories.interpretation: The immediate lesson is not that AI data-centre construction has stopped. It is that local consent has become a material project risk. Developers will need to demonstrate credible community benefits and explain their energy and water plans before expecting approval.
stories.source_title: Amazon's $17bn Ohio AI data centre bet threatened by voter backlash

stories.headline: Reuters traces how Chinese AI developers use US-model outputs
stories.confirmed_fact: Reuters examined more than 300 Chinese research papers, patents, company records and policy documents. It found examples of Chinese teams using outputs from US models, including OpenAI systems, to train smaller domestic models through distillation. Chinese industrial AI policy encourages distillation as a technique, but does not specifically direct companies to distil American models.
stories.why_it_matters: Distillation can transfer selected capabilities into cheaper systems and reduce some computing demands. It does not reproduce every capability of a frontier model or remove the need for advanced chips, and some uses can conflict with model-provider terms.
stories.interpretation: The hardware contest is only part of AI competition: access to high-quality training examples also matters. The evidence supports a growing industrial practice, not the stronger claim that distillation alone explains Chinese model advances or circumvents all export controls.
stories.source_title: China taps US AI models to train homegrown rivals as chip curbs bite

stories.headline: Researcher finds coding-agent indicators in Windows diagnostics
stories.confirmed_fact: Independent researcher Xusheng Li analysed a Windows 11 diagnostics component and demonstrated that it can record whether certain coding agents and developer tools were observed. On a test system with optional diagnostic data enabled, he found a compact usage report queued for Microsoft. The feature was not active in every Windows image he tested.
stories.why_it_matters: Even a simple record of which tools run can reveal workplace preferences. The identified report used tool-presence flags; the investigation did not find prompts or source-code contents in that report.
stories.interpretation: This is a reason to review diagnostic settings, not evidence that every Windows 11 PC is sending coding-agent histories. Users can inspect Settings → Privacy & security → Diagnostics & feedback; organisations should also review managed-device policies.
stories.source_title: Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use

stories.headline: Microsoft details three-factor cause of November email outage
stories.confirmed_fact: Microsoft's preliminary incident report links the 12–13 November disruption to three interacting conditions: a latent defect in a July change to Microsoft 365 gateway servers, extra traffic after a Teams gateway failover, and nearly 14% of gateway capacity being unavailable. Exchange Online mailbox access suffered most; other Microsoft 365 services experienced varying secondary effects.
stories.why_it_matters: The fault survived normal testing and deployment but became disruptive under a workload and hardware combination the tests had not covered. Some services failed over to other gateways, while Exchange Online could not do so at the required scale.
stories.interpretation: Resilience depends on realistic load tests and recovery routes as much as on avoiding code defects. This is a preliminary root-cause account, with a final report expected; it should not be described as a simple July-update failure of all Microsoft services.
stories.source_title: Microsoft blames monster email outage on software defect introduced in July fix

practical_takeaway: If you manage a service that depends on Microsoft 365, check your fallback communication and recovery arrangements rather than assuming one provider will always be accessible. Windows users concerned about developer-tool telemetry can review optional diagnostic data under Settings → Privacy & security → Diagnostics & feedback. Infrastructure planners should include local consent, power and water impacts in project risk assessments.
watch_next: Watch whether Amazon and developers contest or redesign the affected Ohio sites; whether regulators clarify permitted uses of distillation; whether Microsoft comments on the Windows diagnostic feature; and what its final Microsoft 365 incident report adds to the preliminary account.
